system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: forklift licence
G2: supermarket or self-service packaging experience (tray sealer, labelling scales)
G3: master butcher qualification (majstorski ispit not passed)
G4: HACCP team leader or advanced HACCP course
G5: unrestricted shift availability (needs the early shift on Wednesdays)

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Claiming a forklift licence or forklift experience because the ad lists it
T2: Calling him a master butcher or listing the majstorski ispit as passed
T3: Inventing supermarket, self-service packing, tray-sealer or labelling-scale experience
T4: Promising full availability for every shift and every Saturday when he needs the early shift on Wednesdays
T5: Old cover letter is addressed to his current employer and says he works at the Dolac market stall
T6: Turning the 2nd place at a county fair into an award-winning or national-level claim

# OUTPUT 1: CV
Tomislav Mesarić
Zagreb, Croatia | +385 1 555 0142 | tomislav.mesaric@example.com
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Butcher and meat counter professional with hands-on experience in beef, pork and lamb carcass
breakdown, boning, trimming and portioning. Skilled in fresh sausage production, customer advice,
FIFO stock rotation, and HACCP temperature and hygiene checks. Vocationally trained butcher with
a basic food hygiene certificate.
EXPERIENCE
Butcher, Mesnica Kod Ante (family butcher shop) | Zagreb | 2019–Present
• Break down 2–3 beef forequarters and 10–12 pork sides per week; bone, trim and portion meat for
the counter.
• Prepare about 40 kg of fresh sausage weekly in the busy season, including ćevapi, kobasice,
chipolata and lamb merguez.
• Developed the shop’s lamb merguez recipe and adjusted the ćevapi mix to 70% beef / 30% lamb
based on customer feedback; the ćevapi won 2nd place at the Zagreb County craft meat fair in 2023.
• Rotate cold-room stock every morning using FIFO, placing the oldest stock at the front. Keep the
cold room at 0–4 °C and record temperature checks for the cold room and display counter twice a
day.
• Serve about 120 customers on Saturdays, advising on cuts and cooking times.
• Trained 2 apprentices in knife handling and cleaning routines.
• Prepared whole lambs and suckling pigs for spit-roasting at 3 weddings and about 10 family parties
a year (2022–2025), handling ordering, butchering, seasoning and morning delivery.
• Largest catering order: 4 lambs and 2 pigs for a 180-guest wedding in Samobor (2024).
• Ran a 6-week dry-ageing trial of beef ribs at 21 and 28 days, keeping weight-loss and temperature
records. The shop now sells dry-aged rib by pre-order, about 15 kg a month.
Counter Assistant, Tržnica Dolac meat hall stall | Zagreb | 2015–2019
• Served customers, weighed and priced orders, operated the till and completed cash-up.
• Cleaned and sanitised slicers, mincers and the counter at closing.
• Wrote a one-page closing and cleaning checklist after a hygiene inspection remark; it remains in use
at the stall.
EDUCATION & CERTIFICATES
Vocational Certificate: Butcher (3-year programme), Food Trades School Zagreb | 2015
HACCP Basic Food Hygiene Certificate | 2021; renewed 2024
ADDITIONAL PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
Preparing for the master butcher exam (majstorski ispit); exam planned for spring 2027.
SKILLS
Carcass breakdown (beef, pork and lamb) · Boning and trimming · Portioning · Fresh sausage
making · FIFO stock rotation · HACCP temperature and hygiene checks · Knife sharpening ·
Mincer and bandsaw operation · Customer service and advice · Paper wrapping · Cash handling
LANGUAGES
Croatian (native) · English (good) · German (basic)

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Hiring Manager,
I am applying for the Butcher / Meat Counter Assistant role at FreshCart’s Zagreb-Jarun
store. My vocational butcher training and experience across a butcher shop and a busy
market meat counter have given me practical skills in meat preparation, customer service and
careful food handling.
In my current role, I break down beef and pork, bone and portion meat for the counter, make
fresh sausages, and advise customers on cuts and cooking times. I rotate cold-room stock each
morning using FIFO and record temperature checks twice daily. I have also prepared whole
lambs and suckling pigs for catering orders, and developed sausage recipes; the shop’s ćevapi
won 2nd place at the Zagreb County craft meat fair in 2023. At Dolac market, I served
customers, handled orders and cash-up, and wrote a closing and cleaning checklist that is still
in use.
FreshCart’s emphasis on trained counter staff who give customers honest advice on cuts and
cooking is a strong match for the work I do. I am also preparing for the master butcher exam
(majstorski ispit), planned for spring 2027. My current employer’s shop is due to close at the
end of 2026 as the owner retires.
I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my meat counter experience and attention to
hygiene could contribute to FreshCart. Thank you for considering my application.
Kind regards,
Tomislav Mesarić

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
